summary: H.R. 5713 amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to authorize and streamline the expedited removal of non-citizens who are identified as criminal gang members, members of foreign terrorist organizations, or who have been convicted of specific crimes. It transfers certain authorities from the Attorney General to the Secretary of Homeland Security, mandates detention for specified criminal non-citizens, and restricts eligibility for asylum and other forms of immigration relief.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to expedited removal proceedings, mandatory detention, ineligibility for asylum and withholding of removal, and disqualification from other immigration relief.
affected_groups.group: Incarcerated and non-incarcerated non-citizens with specified criminal convictions or gang/terrorist affiliations

affected_groups.effect: Assumes responsibilities for conducting special removal proceedings and managing detention and removal processes previously handled or shared with the Attorney General.

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish special removal proceedings at correctional facilities for incarcerated non-citizens convicted of certain offenses, or determined to be members of criminal gangs, transnational criminal organizations, or foreign terrorist organizations, or convicted of specified felonies, misdemeanors against vulnerable groups, assaults on law enforcement, o
Grants the Secretary of Homeland Security authority previously held by the Attorney General regarding special removal proceedings and administrative discretion.
Mandates the detention of inadmissible or deportable non-citizens who belong to criminal gangs or transnational criminal organizations, or who have been convicted of specified offenses.
Makes non-citizens who fall under the bill's expanded criminal and gang definitions ineligible for withholding of removal under section 241(b)(3)(B).
Denies asylum eligibility to non-citizens convicted of the offenses or meeting the criteria described in the bill's expanded provisions.
Bars impacted non-citizens from receiving any other relief under immigration laws.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 5713 amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to authorize and streamline the expedited removal of non-citizens who are identified as criminal gang members, members of foreign terrorist organizations, or who have been convicted of specific crimes. It transfers certain authorities from the Attorney General to the Secretary of Homeland Security, mandates detention for specified criminal non-citizens, and restricts eligibility for asylum and other forms of immigration relief.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters federal immigration enforcement by broadening the scope of individuals subject to expedited removal, mandating detention for wider categories of non-citizens with criminal histories or gang associations, and removing eligibility for multiple forms of humanitarian and immigration relief.
